fact: The brightest star of the Great Bear, first in the handle of the Big Dipper.
bio: Alioth (Epsilon Ursae Majoris) is a peculiar white star about 81 light-years away, the brightest in Ursa Major. Its spectrum shows odd, shifting chemical signatures tied to a strong magnetic field.
cultural: The name derives from Arabic. As the first star in the handle of the Big Dipper — or the tail of the Great Bear — Alioth is a fixture of northern navigation and one of the 57 stars used in celestial position-finding.
